heroTitle: I build the data layer, and the models that earn a place on top of it.
heroLead: Nine years moving numbers from source systems to the people who act on them — warehouse modelling, orchestration, and the analytics and machine-learning layer above. The work is filed in five modules; read whichever one you came for.
aboutTitle: I make data trustworthy, then make it useful.
about:
I am Keyur — a data analytics engineer who has spent nine years moving numbers from source systems to the people who act on them. That has meant modelling warehouses, orchestrating loads and writing the tests that catch a broken join before a director does; increasingly it has meant the machine-learning layer on top — propensity models, vision at the edge, and retrieval systems that can cite their sources.

I keep the work filed in five modules on purpose. AI and deep learning are where the newest questions live; machine learning, data analytics and data engineering are the ground they stand on. I do not think you can do one well while treating the others as someone else's problem.

When something works, it is usually because the boring parts were done first: a defined grain, a nightly test, a number someone can verify by hand. I write about that on the blog, and the receipts are in the projects.
